regulations: Act on Recycling of End-of-Life Vehicles
Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act
regulation.activity: Launching a new electric vehicle (EV) production line and exporting units to the European Union and United States.
regulation.parties_involved: Suzuki Motor Corporation (Japan HQ), EV battery suppliers (China), third-party manufacturing contractors, logistics/export partners, dealerships in EU and US, end customers, cloud service providers (data processing)

risk_factors: Execution of U.S. tariffs on automobiles as of April 2025.
Dependence on Chinese battery suppliers potentially subject to the updated September 2025 End User List.
Strict data processing and cybersecurity requirements for Software Defined Vehicles (SDV).
risk_analysis.risk_summary: The primary compliance risks are centered on the 2025 U.S. automotive tariffs and the enhanced Japanese export control regime (FEFTA) which restricts sensitive EV-related technology transfers. The involvement of Chinese battery suppliers and cloud-based data processing adds significant exposure to restricted entity lists and new digital mobility standards.
violations_detected: Potential violation of updated FEFTA (April 2025) regarding EV technology exports — source: https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2025/0404_001.html
Potential non-compliance with new SDV data standards in Mobility DX Strategy — source: https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2025/0609_001.html
override_log: Finding level CRITICAL detected — risk level upgraded from HIGH to CRITICAL.

confidence.disclaimer: ✅  No assumption-based statements detected. Analysis references verified regulatory sources.

findings.finding: Planned exports to the United States are subject to new tariff measures announced by METI in April 2025.
Chinese battery suppliers require re-validation against the updated September 2025 End User List to avoid FEFTA violations.
findings.related_regulation: Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act

findings.finding: Cloud-based data processing for the new EV line must be updated to comply with the June 2025 Mobility DX Strategy for SDVs.

recommendations.action: Engage METI Consultation Counters regarding U.S. tariff impact and cash flow support.
Conduct a comprehensive KYC audit of all Chinese battery suppliers against the September 2025 End User List.
Align EV cloud data protocols with the June 2025 Mobility DX Strategy standards for cybersecurity and data infrastructure.

compliance_report.executive_summary: Suzuki's EV expansion is currently challenged by a rapidly evolving regulatory landscape, notably the execution of U.S. automotive tariffs and stricter Japanese export controls implemented in 2025. Immediate attention is required to re-verify Chinese supply chain partners against the newly updated End User List and to adapt data governance to the 2025 Mobility DX Strategy. Proactive engagement with METI's support task force is recommended to mitigate trade risks associated with the U.S. market.

regulation_monitor.monitor_notes: Recent amendments to the Foreign Exchange Order (April 2025) and the updated End User List (September 2025) significantly tighten controls on cross-border technology transfers and supply chain partners. The establishment of a METI task force for U.S. automotive tariffs (April 2025) signals a major change in the trade environment for Japanese vehicle exports.
